append.text: **Ps 88:6 — with an accusative of the thing (*Confitebúntur cæli mirabília tua … étenim veritátem tuam*) → *Os céus darão graças pelas vossas maravilhas … e também pela vossa verdade*** — 70:22's *por* build. The Latinist (minor, v1) asked for *celebrarão*, to keep the accusative; that was refused for D5, and *celebrarão* is option 1 of Ps 88's `conf6`.

**Ps 88:27 *suscéptor salútis meæ* → *o amparo da minha salvação*** (the row). **88:19 *assúmptio nostra* (ἀντίλημψις, the same Greek root) → *o nosso amparo*** too, on D15's Greek test. The Latinist (v1 and v2, minor) asked for *acolhimento* to keep the two Latin words apart; it is held as an option (Ps 88 `assump`).

**Ps 88:32 *Si justítias meas profanáverint* (δικαιώματα) → *Se profanarem as minhas justiças*** — the row kept while it is open. The blind reader did not hear it as 'statutes'. *os meus preceitos* is option 1 of Ps 88's `j32`: the place this row said 'may want *preceitos*'. No Latinist remark.

**Ps 88:11 people → *dispersastes os vossos inimigos*.** **88:34 *Misericórdiam … non dispérgam ab eo* (διασκεδάσω) → *não dissiparei dele a minha misericórdia*** (the v1 Latinist): *dispersar* does not take *misericórdia* in Portuguese, and *dissipar* keeps the scattering. Draft 1 had *retirarei* (MS1932), now an option.

**Ps 88:51 *quod contínui in sinu meo* (ὑπέσχον) → *que … guardei no meu seio*** — draft 1 had the row's *contive*. The stylist and the blind reader both heard it as 'I restrained', so it is now an option of Ps 88's `ct51`.
**Ps 88:39 *distulísti Christum tuum* (ἀνεβάλου) → *adiastes o vosso Cristo*** — the row. Both Latinist gates passed it. The blind reader heard 'postponed Christ' (D19 on purpose).

**Ps 88:52 *commutatiónem Christi tui* → *a mudança do vosso Cristo*** — the 'own look' this row asked for. It is the local sense of 54:20b (DRB 'change', MS1932), and *a troca* is the option. Both Latinist gates passed it; the blind reader found the line incomprehensible whichever word is used.

**Ps 88:41 *posuísti firmaméntum ejus formídinem* (ὀχυρώματα, of the king) → *fizestes da sua fortaleza um pavor*** — decided locally (D31). *fortaleza* holds both 'stronghold' and 'firmness'; *firmeza* (72:4) is an option. No Latinist remark.

**Ps 88:13 *tuum brácchium cum poténtia* → *vosso é o braço com potência*** — the row. The stylist asked for *poderio* ('com potência' sounded technical); that was refused. The Latinist's verbless form is an option.

terms: | præparáre (ἑτοιμάζω, *kûn*) · præparátio | preparar · preparação (*a vossa verdade será preparada neles*; *Para todo o sempre prepararei a tua descendência*; *a justiça e o juízo são a preparação do vosso trono*) | open | Ps 88:3, 4, 14: the psalm's one verb kept three times (rule 6). Also 22:5, 64:7, 67:11. The blind reader heard 'get ready', a weaker sense than 'establish'. *firmar … a base* and MS1932's three words (*solidamente estabelecida*, *conservarei*, *a base*) are options of Ps 88's `praep`. No Latinist remark. |

| beneplácitum (noun, εὐδοκία) | favor (*e no vosso favor será exaltado o nosso chifre*) | open | Ps 88:18 (v2). Draft 1 had *beneplácito*: the stylist called it chancery Latin, and the blind reader did not know it. *boa vontade* is *bona volúntas*'s word (5:13b, 50:20). Options: *beneplácito*, *agrado*. Nine more verses have the noun (grep): check them before settling. |

| sepes (φραγμοί) | cercas (*Destruístes todas as suas cercas*) | open | Ps 88:41 (v2). Draft 1 had *sebes*, to keep it apart from 79:13 *macéria → cerca*, but the blind reader did not know *sebes*. The cost is that *cerca* now serves both words. |

| verbera (μάστιγες) | açoites (*e com açoites os seus pecados*) | open | Ps 88:33, from MS1932. It is kept apart from *plaga/flagéllum → flagelo* (D39); *flagelos* is the option. The blind reader listed *açoites* as unknown, and it was kept as a register word. |

| *Si … méntiar* (oath formula) · *in sancto meo* (swearing) | *não mentirei a …* · *pela minha santidade* | open | Ps 88:36. The Hebrew oath form ('if I lie' = 'I will not lie') would be heard in Portuguese as a condition with the opposite sense, so grammar yields (D2). DRB and MS1932 have the same. Both Latinist gates asked, minor, for *se eu mentir a Davi!*, and the v2 gate also asked for *pelo meu santo*. Both were held as options. 59:8 *in sancto suo* with *falou* stays *no seu santo*. |
formulas: | *Misericórdias Dómini in ætérnum cantábo: in generatiónem et generatiónem annuntiábo veritátem tuam in ore meo* (88:2–2b; missa Sancti 07-01 and others — grep) · *Invéni David servum meum: óleo sancto meo unxi eum. Manus enim mea auxiliábitur ei … Nihil profíciet inimícus in eo, et fílius iniquitátis non nocébit ei* (88:21–23; graduals and responsories, Commune C4) · *V. Ipse invocábit me. R. Pater meus es tu* (88:27; Christmas Matins, horas Sancti 12-25) · *Semel jurávi in sancto meo: Semen ejus in ætérnum manébit …* (88:36–38 without *Si David méntiar*; responsory, Commune C2) | *As misericórdias do Senhor * cantarei para sempre. De geração em geração * anunciarei a vossa verdade com a minha boca* · *Encontrei Davi, meu servo: * com o meu óleo santo o ungi. Pois a minha mão o ajudará …* (the responsory's *non nocébit ei* → *não lhe fará mal*) · *V. Ele me invocará. R. Tu és meu Pai* (D17: the address follows the speaker; *Vós sois meu Pai* is the option) · *Uma vez jurei pela minha santidade: * a sua descendência permanecerá para sempre* | open — Ps 88; each colon reads alone |
